title: Past action and the requirement of exchange
shortTitle: Past action and the requirement of exchange
summary: An act completed before a later promise ordinarily cannot be the bargained-for return for that promise, because the later promise did not seek the completed act in exchange.
notes:
Feinberg’s years of prior service explained the employer’s gratitude but did not themselves establish an exchange for its later pension promise. The retirement decision required its own analysis under promissory estoppel. The syllabus separately assigns New York General Obligations Law § 5-1105, whose signed-writing requirements provide a distinct statutory route for certain promises based on past consideration. Read that provision on the supplement page rather than assuming that merely mentioning past services always suffices.

Feinberg’s past service explains the employer’s generosity but was not induced by the later pension. Her additional eighteen months of service were likewise not demanded by the resolution as its price. The problem concerning a benefactor’s past gift and a later naming assurance asks about timing and separate promises. The first page of Mills introduces moral obligation, but the remainder of that opinion is outside the assigned ranges.
